41b020c80f528194b2bdf727773b9dce:
DISSIPATE No. 8 OF NINE NEVADA DEPRESSIONS — Michael Heizer, 1968.

Five shallow trenches lined with wood, cut into the dry lakebed of Black Rock Desert in Nevada and placed as if matches had been dropped on the ground. Part of a series of nine works across the Nevada desert, made to be eroded and lost. Land art at its beginning: sculpture made by taking material away.

#michaelheizer #landart #nevada #desert #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528110ab4de4be027d17e7:
LE CHÂTEAU DES PYRÉNÉES — René Magritte, 1959.

A huge boulder hangs above a stormy sea, with a small castle growing out of its top. Magritte paints the impossible with the calm precision of a postcard, so that gravity seems to be the thing that is wrong. The painting is in the Israel Museum, Jerusalem.

#renemagritte #surrealism #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528159bd29d44330043cc3:
IL MONUMENTO CONTINUO — Superstudio, 1969.

A single gridded structure that wraps the whole planet, crossing deserts, cities and seas without changing. The Florentine group drew it in collages as a critique of architecture's will to order everything. One of the founding images of Radical Architecture.

#superstudio #radicalarchitecture #collage #utopia #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281abb253febb7d4c767e:
STRIKE: TO ROBERTA AND RUDY — Richard Serra, 1969–71.

A single plate of hot-rolled steel, eight by twenty-four feet, wedged into the corner of a room and held there only by the two walls. It cuts the space in two, and as you walk around it the plate turns from surface to edge and back. Now at the Guggenheim, New York.

#richardserra #sculpture #steel #minimalism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52810f888fcaa6e003f4d6:
RODEN CRATER — James Turrell, since 1979.

An extinct volcanic cone in the Painted Desert of Arizona, bought by Turrell in 1979 and reshaped from inside into an observatory for the naked eye. Tunnels and chambers frame the sky, the sun and the moon. Still in progress after more than four decades.

#jamesturrell #rodencrater #landart #light #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528197842cc4c143d6ddd4:
THE ELEMENTAL HOUSE — Charles Jencks with Buzz Yudell and Charles Moore, 1982. Rustic Canyon, Los Angeles.

A 1950s ranch house reworked around the four elements, earth, water, air and fire. Its pool is shaped like the State of California. Postmodern symbolism, played with a straight face.

#charlesjencks #buzzyudell #postmodernism #losangeles #pool #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818a82ffca621a4a5dff:
MODULAR CUBE — Sol LeWitt, 1965.

An open lattice of identical square cells, the same in every direction. LeWitt chose the cube because it is the least expressive form there is, and so it lets the system be the subject. The idea is the machine that makes the art.

#sollewitt #minimalism #conceptualart #sculpture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281b8b4befdbfa6a38214:
ARCHITECTURE OBLIQUE — Claude Parent, 1960s–70s.

With Paul Virilio, Parent proposed living on inclined planes instead of flat floors: walking would become climbing, and the body would feel every move. Built examples are few, the church of Sainte-Bernadette in Nevers (1966) among them, but the drawings remain.

#claudeparent #paulvirilio #functionoblique #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281c0a2ccc646943ab3ed:
BURGERWEESHUIS (AMSTERDAM ORPHANAGE) — Aldo van Eyck, 1955–1960.

A small city for children: repeated domed units grouped in clusters, with interior streets and courtyards between them. Van Eyck called it a house like a small city and a city like a large house. A founding work of Dutch Structuralism.

#aldovaneyck #structuralism #amsterdam #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281abb7eee7eecf4a6da9:
WEISS AUF SCHWARZ (WHITE ON BLACK) — Wassily Kandinsky, 1930.

Painted in his last years at the Bauhaus in Dessau: thin, floating geometric shapes on a black ground. For Kandinsky black was a silence without future, against which every color sounds sharper.

#wassilykandinsky #bauhaus #abstraction #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528197a3cdc5169ebb2d78:
NO-STOP CITY — Archizoom Associati, 1969–1972.

An endless, homogeneous interior, lit and air-conditioned like a supermarket, where furniture and tents replace buildings. Archizoom drew it with a typewriter, as a grid of characters, to show the city as pure quantity. A radical critique of the modern metropolis.

#archizoom #nostopcity #radicalarchitecture #andreabranzi #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281058789c1db3c70594b:
THE INCOMPLETE TRUTH — Damien Hirst, 2006.

A white dove with spread wings, suspended in formaldehyde inside a glass and steel case. The sign of the Holy Spirit and of peace becomes a specimen.

#damienhirst #formaldehyde #contemporaryart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a89843d0fb13ce12c9:
CONCETTO SPAZIALE, ATTESE — Lucio Fontana, 1963.

A monochrome canvas opened by clean cuts with a blade. Fontana's slashes are not destruction but an opening onto the space behind the painting. 'Attese' means waitings.

#luciofontana #spazialismo #concettospaziale #italianart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281829890dbabe9980e18:
TEATRO DEL MONDO — Aldo Rossi, 1979–80.

A floating wooden theatre built for the Venice Biennale, towed across the lagoon on a barge and moored in front of the Punta della Dogana. It belonged to the city for one season, then it was dismantled. Rossi's most poetic building, made to disappear.

#aldorossi #teatrodelmondo #venezia #biennale #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528177b6cfe26e348c0d0d:
STILL LIFE — Tom Wesselmann, 1962.

From the series of Still Lifes begun in 1962: collage and paint on board, with supermarket products and advertising images arranged like a Dutch still life. American abundance seen in the flat language of the billboard.

#tomwesselmann #popart #stilllife #collage #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816b8ad0c36b54152947:
BARCELONA PAVILION — Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, 1929.

German pavilion for the International Exposition in Barcelona: free-standing walls of onyx and green marble, chromed cruciform columns, and a reflecting pool. Demolished in 1930 and rebuilt on the same site in 1986.

#miesvanderrohe #barcelonapavilion #modernism #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a78b58eb442374f9b9:
STILL LIFE WITH GOLDFISH — Roy Lichtenstein, 1972.

Lichtenstein quotes Matisse's goldfish bowl and translates it into Ben-Day dots, black outlines and flat color. Painting about painting, in the language of comic strips.

#roylichtenstein #popart #matisse #stilllife #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528151b99cc959790f273e:
THE BIG DUCK — Flanders, Long Island, New York, 1931.

A building in the shape of a duck, built by a duck farmer to sell ducks and eggs. Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown and Steven Izenour used it in Learning from Las Vegas (1972) as their 'duck': a building whose form is its sign, against the 'decorated shed'.

#bigduck #venturiscottbrown #learningfromlasvegas #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d097bae2bf94d827c9:
BAUHAUS — Herbert Bayer, 1925.

Bayer studied at the Bauhaus in Weimar and in 1925 became head of the new printing and advertising workshop in Dessau. He designed the 'universal' alphabet in lower case only. Typography reduced to geometry.

#herbertbayer #bauhaus #typography #graphicdesign #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528195921efeead1ecc049:
SCANDIANO — Luigi Ghirri, 1971.

Ghirri was born in Scandiano, near Reggio Emilia, and began photographing in the early 1970s, while still working as a surveyor. His Emilia is made of signs, walls and empty corners, looked at with quiet attention.

#luigighirri #fotografia #emilia #italianphotography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528116a057fbc81ff022db:
HOUSE AT MINAMI-AOYAMA — Kunihiko Hayakawa, Tokyo.

Hayakawa built his architecture around the 'landscapes that architecture produces' in the city. His Tokyo houses read like fragments of stage set, layered planes and colors in a dense, fragmented city.

#kunihikohayakawa #tokyo #japanesearchitecture #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52813781cbf2465577559b:
I AM A MONUMENT — Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown, 1972.

A drawing from Learning from Las Vegas: a plain shed with a huge sign that announces 'I am a monument'. The decorated shed, where the meaning is written on the building rather than built into it.

#venturiscottbrown #learningfromlasvegas #decoratedshed #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f1885fd46b51436404:
CARCERI D'INVENZIONE, PLATE VII — Giovanni Battista Piranesi, c. 1745–1761.

The Drawbridge: stairs, bridges and walkways climb through a vast, impossible prison. The Carceri were first etched around 1745–50 and reworked, darker and deeper, in 1761.

#piranesi #carceri #etching #imaginaryarchitecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528127b663eb3ea3abe386:
PARTHENOPE — Paolo Sorrentino, 2024.

Born in the sea off Naples in 1950, Parthenope crosses decades of the city's beauty and decay. Sorrentino films Naples the way he films his heroine: sunlit, theatrical, always slightly out of reach. Cinematography by Daria D'Antonio.

#mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d186a0c7e297e33f9f:
PARC DE LA VILLETTE — OMA / Rem Koolhaas, 1982. Paris.

OMA's competition entry for a park on the site of the old Paris slaughterhouses: the ground cut into parallel strips, each one a different programme, laid side by side like the floors of a skyscraper turned on its side. The competition was won by Bernard Tschumi, but the strips became one of the most copied diagrams in architecture.

#oma #remkoolhaas #parcdelavillette #paris #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281418941f9ee6e59a263:
SESC POMPÉIA — Lina Bo Bardi, 1977–1986. São Paulo.

An old drum factory turned into a leisure centre, kept almost as it was found. Next to it, two concrete towers joined by flying walkways, with windows like holes torn in the walls. Bo Bardi called it a citadel of freedom.

#linabobardi #sescpompeia #saopaulo #brutalism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281b3beb2dc01d8747dfc:
PLAN OF A TOWN — Paul Klee, 1930.

A city reduced to a few lines, blocks and signs, somewhere between a map and a piece of music. Klee taught at the Bauhaus until 1931 and drew cities as if they were written.

#paulklee #bauhaus #drawing #city #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528196a41ce1e35ea5cf62:
WOHNHAUS SCHLESISCHES TOR (BONJOUR TRISTESSE) — Álvaro Siza, 1982–1984. Berlin.

A housing block on a corner of Kreuzberg, built for the IBA. Its long curved façade follows the street without a single gesture of style. Someone painted 'Bonjour Tristesse' on the roof parapet, and the name stayed.

#alvarosiza #bonjourtristesse #berlin #kreuzberg #iba #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52814f83c5c89c264f0e4e:
TOMBA BRION — Carlo Scarpa, 1969–1978. San Vito d'Altivole.

A cemetery garden for the Brion family, with pools, a chapel and an arched shelter over the graves. Two interlocking circles in the wall look onto the fields. Scarpa is buried here, just outside the walls.

#carloscarpa #tombabrion #brion #italianarchitecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812ebc37d9ce3972dde7:
COMPOSITION N. 17 — Jean Gorin, 1961.

Gorin met Mondrian in Paris in the 1920s and spent his life carrying Neo-Plasticism into relief: primary colors, black lines and white planes that step forward from the wall.

#jeangorin #neoplasticism #abstraction #relief #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281998fb9eba463f5e920:
THE CREATION OF ADAM — Michelangelo, c. 1512. Sistine Chapel, Rome.

Part of the ceiling Michelangelo painted between 1508 and 1512. God reaches toward Adam, who lifts his hand lazily back; between the two fingers, a gap of a few centimetres that holds the whole image.

#michelangelo #sistinechapel #creationofadam #renaissance #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52814fba09f088c3f9ab88:
MARILYN'S LIPS — Andy Warhol, 1962.

A wall of silkscreened mouths, taken from a publicity still of Marilyn Monroe and repeated until the face disappears. Made in the months after her death in August 1962. Hirshhorn Museum, Washington.

#andywarhol #marilynmonroe #popart #silkscreen #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812f9ebace273681e1fa:
STILL LIFE — David LaChapelle, 2012.

LaChapelle photographed wax figures of celebrities and politicians after they were damaged in transport: broken heads, faces cracked open. Fame turned into a pile of fragments.

#davidlachapelle #stilllife #photography #wax #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528191ba2dd5bdec5d999f:
CIDADE DE DEUS (CITY OF GOD) — Fernando Meirelles, Kátia Lund, 2002.

The story of a Rio de Janeiro favela from the 1960s to the 1980s, told by a boy who becomes a photographer. Shot with many non-professional actors from the favelas, it moves at the speed of the violence it shows.

#cityofgod #fernandomeirelles #brazil #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f1baa6d563212c4ca5:
JACKSON POLLOCK — Hans Namuth, 1950.

Namuth photographed Pollock painting in his barn studio in Springs, Long Island, moving around a canvas laid on the floor. These photographs and Namuth's film turned the act of painting into the image everyone remembers.

#hansnamuth #jacksonpollock #actionpainting #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812b9413c9b388559eaf:
FIRENZE (FLOODED FLORENCE) — Superstudio, 1972.

From the series 'Salvataggi di centri storici': Florence filled with water up to the cupola of the Duomo, which stands out of the lake like an island. Made a few years after the real flood of 1966, as an ironic proposal to 'save' the city.

#superstudio #firenze #radicalarchitecture #collage #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f08370f65e81d74889:
GERMANIA ANNO ZERO — Roberto Rossellini, 1948.

A boy wanders through the ruins of Berlin after the war. Shot on location among the bombed buildings, it closes Rossellini's war trilogy after Roma città aperta and Paisà.

#robertorossellini #germaniaannozero #neorealism #berlin #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812fbf5ef8ea9751cec8:
HAND WITH REFLECTING SPHERE — M. C. Escher, 1935.

A lithograph in which Escher holds a mirrored ball and draws himself reflected in it, with his whole room curving around him. The artist always stays at the centre of the sphere, whichever way he turns.

#mcescher #lithograph #selfportrait #reflection #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a99847c0dcb06dbe6f:
ЧЕЛОВЕК С КИНОАППАРАТОМ (MAN WITH A MOVIE CAMERA) — Dziga Vertov, 1929.

A day in a Soviet city, filmed without actors, script or intertitles. Vertov and his editor Elizaveta Svilova show the camera, the cameraman and the editing table as part of the film itself.

#dzigavertov #manwithamoviecamera #sovietcinema #avantgarde #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528166b9ffc9bb1652f486:
LA JETÉE — Chris Marker, 1962.

A 28-minute film made almost only of still photographs. A man is sent back from a ruined Paris to a memory of a woman on the observation pier at Orly. In one single shot, she moves.

#chrismarker #lajetee #photoroman #frenchcinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281db8a0ee90da4247667:
MAISON DOM-INO — Le Corbusier, 1914.

Three concrete slabs, six thin columns and a stair: a frame for houses to be built quickly after the war. Walls no longer carry anything, so plan and façade become free. The skeleton of modern architecture.

#lecorbusier #domino #modernism #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528125b086dd322a777d80:
IN WEELDE SIET TOE (BEWARE OF LUXURY) — Jan Steen, 1663. Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

A household falls apart while the mother sleeps: a child smokes, a dog eats the pie, a pig wanders in with the tap. The title is a Dutch proverb, and every detail is a moral warning painted with obvious pleasure.

#jansteen #dutchgoldenage #kunsthistorischesmuseum #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528151816ecb8b3c4aeb6a:
KOYAANISQATSI — Godfrey Reggio, 1982.

A film without words: landscapes, cities, crowds and machines, slowed down or sped up, set to the music of Philip Glass. The title is a Hopi word for 'life out of balance'. Cinematography by Ron Fricke.

#koyaanisqatsi #godfreyreggio #philipglass #documentary #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528164a595e2277e9a67b7:
8½ — Federico Fellini, 1963.

A film director who cannot make his film, caught between memories, women and producers. Fellini turned his own creative block into the film, and ended it with everyone holding hands in a circle.

#federicofellini #8andahalf #marcellomastroianni #italiancinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528180a262c1bb3689fcfc:
OLD MAN AT A WINDOW — Samuel van Hoogstraten, 1653. Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

A man leans out of a painted window, so precisely rendered that the frame seems to be part of the wall. Hoogstraten, a pupil of Rembrandt, was a master of trompe-l'œil and of perspective boxes.

#samuelvanhoogstraten #trompeloeil #dutchgoldenage #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528193be4adf14e70ca0af:
ZABRISKIE POINT — Michelangelo Antonioni, 1970.

Antonioni's American film, made in the desert of Death Valley. It ends with a villa exploding again and again in slow motion, and everything it held, clothes, food, books, floating in the sky.

#michelangeloantonioni #zabriskiepoint #deathvalley #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281c983fff8882b07c8a3:
4'33" — John Cage, 1952.

Three movements in which the performer plays nothing. At its first performance in Woodstock, the pianist David Tudor opened and closed the lid of the piano to mark them. The music is whatever sound happens in the room.

#johncage #433 #silence #avantgarde #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52813e8c54e223b46aaab9:
COLD STREAM — Cy Twombly, 1966.

One of the 'blackboard' paintings: loops of white line run across a grey ground like handwriting on a school slate, repeated until they become a current.

#cytwombly #coldstream #blackboardpaintings #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a7ba76fca008d90f78:
TV MURDER IN A HOTEL ON THE CROISETTE — Helmut Newton, 1975.

A staged scene in a hotel room in Cannes: fashion photography that borrows the look of a crime still. Newton made glamour cold, theatrical and slightly dangerous.

#helmutnewton #cannes #fashionphotography #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a4bdabf2a3dd08b32b:
REAR WINDOW — Alfred Hitchcock, 1954.

A photographer with a broken leg watches the courtyard of his building in Greenwich Village and becomes convinced that a neighbour has committed a murder. The whole film was shot on one huge set, a cross-section of windows.

#alfredhitchcock #rearwindow #jamesstewart #gracekelly #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52817fb61dc7659e7bf6f5:
THE WATERS OF LETHE BY THE PLAINS OF ELYSIUM — John Roddam Spencer Stanhope, 1880. Manchester Art Gallery.

Souls in white robes walk down to the river of forgetting before entering paradise. A painting of the second Pre-Raphaelite generation, close to Burne-Jones in its long figures and pale light.

#spencerstanhope #prerafaelites #manchesterartgallery #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a9b18ed9ebd1901eca:
DIRTY WINDOWS — Merry Alpern, 1993–94.

From a friend's apartment, Alpern photographed through the bathroom window of a club in Lower Manhattan. Grainy, cropped by the window frame, the pictures make the viewer a voyeur too.

#merryalpern #dirtywindows #newyork #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528122967fd8249023eaaf:
THE VILLAGE LAWYER — Pieter Brueghel the Younger, c. 1618.

Peasants bring eggs and chickens as payment to a lawyer buried in paper. Brueghel the Younger painted many versions of this scene, a satire on bureaucracy that sold well then and still works.

#pieterbrueghel #villagelawyer #flemishpainting #genrepainting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528199bc1bcfd76d6b1d23:
MANHATTAN — Woody Allen, 1979.

A love letter to New York shot in black and white by Gordon Willis, set to Gershwin. The best-known image: two figures on a bench at dawn, under the Queensboro Bridge.

#woodyallen #manhattan #gordonwillis #newyork #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281fdb89ec8c9dce43b8a:
99 CENT — Andreas Gursky, 1999.

The inside of a discount supermarket in Los Angeles, photographed from above and digitally reworked so that every shelf is equally sharp. Abundance becomes an abstract pattern.

#andreasgursky #99cent #photography #consumerism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528148ab28ccd236b3dc27:
PALAZZO DEL LAVORO — Pier Luigi Nervi, 1959–1961. Turin.

Built for Italia '61, the exhibition for the centenary of Italian unity. The huge square hall is covered by sixteen independent umbrellas: a concrete column that opens at the top into a crown of steel ribs.

#pierluiginervi #palazzodellavoro #torino #italia61 #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281feae34c3de3bf879c7:
UNTITLED (HALLOWEEN) — Diane Arbus, 1970–71.

From Arbus's last series, photographed at Halloween parties and picnics in residences for people with intellectual disabilities. Masks, costumes and open fields; the photographs were printed after her death.

#dianearbus #untitled #photography #americanphotography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528131a874cda47131b5ee:
DENKMAL FÜR DIE ERMORDETEN JUDEN EUROPAS — Peter Eisenman, 2005. Berlin.

2,711 concrete blocks of different heights on a sloping field near the Brandenburg Gate. Walking in, the ground sinks and the blocks rise above your head: a place without a centre, where you lose the others.

#petereisenman #holocaustmemorial #berlin #memorial #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52814b80e4d9f804eedc1d:
PIANTA DI ROMA — Giovanni Battista Piranesi, 1756.

From Le Antichità Romane, Piranesi's four volumes on the ruins of ancient Rome. The plan of the city becomes a fragment of stone itself, drawn as if it were carved and broken.

#piranesi #antichitaromane #roma #etching #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281879c90d98b434e37a8:
THE NIGHT WATCH — Rembrandt van Rijn, 1642. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

The militia company of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, painted not standing in rows but in the middle of moving off. A girl lit up in gold and the captain's hand reaching out are the brightest points in the shadow.

#rembrandt #nightwatch #rijksmuseum #dutchgoldenage #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d8aaf9efa080b53011:
BLOSSOM RESTAURANT, 103 BOWERY — Berenice Abbott, 1935.

From 'Changing New York', Abbott's survey of the city in the 1930s. Every inch of the restaurant front is covered in hand-painted prices and dishes: a façade made of words.

#bereniceabbott #changingnewyork #bowery #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281348c2acaf27206ef75:
FOUNTAIN — Marcel Duchamp, 1917.

A porcelain urinal, turned on its back and signed 'R. Mutt'. Submitted to an exhibition that was supposed to accept everything, and refused. The original was lost; the art world never recovered.

#marcelduchamp #fountain #readymade #dada #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52811ab7c9eb5bce1e0e58:
MAGNETIC VORTICES — René Descartes, 1644.

From the Principia philosophiae: the space around a magnet drawn as a field of swirling particles, threaded through the earth. A diagram of an invisible force, almost two centuries before Faraday's field lines.

#renedescartes #principiaphilosophiae #magnetism #historyofscience #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812bb676e93828097a4d:
THE CITY OF THE CAPTIVE GLOBE — Rem Koolhaas with Madelon Vriesendorp, 1972.

A grid of blocks, each one a different ideology built as a tower, with a globe suspended at the centre. Later published in Delirious New York (1978), Koolhaas's 'retroactive manifesto' for Manhattan.

#remkoolhaas #madelonvriesendorp #deliriousnewyork #oma #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528122b04dcd821dda95c7:
THE GODFATHER — Francis Ford Coppola, 1972.

The Corleone family, from the wedding in the garden to the closing door. Gordon Willis lit it so darkly that he was nicknamed 'the Prince of Darkness': faces emerge from shadow as in an old painting.

#francisfordcoppola #thegodfather #gordonwillis #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52815db5b1c6eedaec3110:
A SUDDEN GUST OF WIND (AFTER HOKUSAI) — Jeff Wall, 1993. Tate, London.

A large lightbox photograph restaging a print by Hokusai in a field near Vancouver. It looks like a single instant, but it was assembled from many photographs taken over months.

#jeffwall #hokusai #tate #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281138f75cc65d45ed554:
DER WANDERER ÜBER DEM NEBELMEER — Caspar David Friedrich, c. 1818. Hamburger Kunsthalle.

A man seen from behind stands on a rock above a sea of fog. We see what he sees, and we cannot see his face. The image of the Romantic individual in front of nature.

#caspardavidfriedrich #wanderer #romanticism #kunsthalle #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52819ea1fcc9e8747826d8:
UNIVERSALIS COSMOGRAPHIA — Martin Waldseemüller, 1507.

The first map to use the name 'America', given to the new lands in honour of Amerigo Vespucci. Printed in twelve sheets; the only known surviving copy is in the Library of Congress.

#waldseemuller #america #cartography #historyofscience #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816b91abfbd4c3bb1ef4:
THE SEVEN HEAVENLY PALACES — Anselm Kiefer.

Kiefer's seven towers of stacked concrete containers were built in 2004 in a former factory in Milan, now Pirelli HangarBicocca. The name comes from the Sefer Hechalot, a Hebrew mystical text about the ascent to heaven.

#anselmkiefer #sevenheavenlypalaces #hangarbicocca #milano #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281b99242da30cb3ec2f8:
DOWN BY LAW — Jim Jarmusch, 1986.

Three men share a cell in a New Orleans prison, then escape through the swamps of Louisiana. Black and white photography by Robby Müller, with Tom Waits, John Lurie and Roberto Benigni.

#jimjarmusch #downbylaw #robbymuller #tomwaits #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281ec8608d8ce62c79648:
IL TEATRO DELLA MEMORIA — Giulio Camillo, c. 1550.

A wooden theatre in which the spectator stands on the stage and looks at the seats, where the whole of knowledge is arranged in images. Camillo described it in L'idea del theatro, published in 1550; the theatre itself was never completed.

#giuliocamillo #teatrodellamemoria #artofmemory #renaissance #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281c0aabbd6a71f6f53fe:
LAS MENINAS — Diego Velázquez, 1656. Museo del Prado, Madrid.

The Infanta Margarita and her ladies-in-waiting, Velázquez at his canvas, and in the mirror at the back the king and queen. The painting looks at us from the place where the royal couple stands.

#velazquez #lasmeninas #museodelprado #baroque #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816d84f7fee126ca2439:
ANTHROPOMÉTRIES — Yves Klein, 1960.

Models covered in Klein's patented blue paint pressed their bodies on paper, while musicians played his 'Monotone-Silence Symphony'. The body became a living brush.

#yvesklein #anthropometries #internationalkleinblue #performance #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818190ffe6480bae7d6a:
MAGNET TV — Nam June Paik, 1965. Whitney Museum, New York.

A television set with a large magnet placed on top: moving it bends the electron beam and turns the picture into abstract shapes. One of the first works of video art.

#namjunepaik #magnettv #videoart #whitneymuseum #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528171b7b7e5ac6b437a5b:
VIDEODROME — David Cronenberg, 1983.

A cable TV programmer discovers a signal that changes the bodies of those who watch it. Television becomes flesh, and the screen breathes.

#davidcronenberg #videodrome #bodyhorror #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818c9256ee0f61cd76d5:
THE NAKED KISS — Samuel Fuller, 1964.

It opens with a woman beating a man, and her wig coming off. A former prostitute tries to start again in a small town that hides much worse. Fuller's B movie, as hard as a headline.

#samuelfuller #thenakedkiss #filmnoir #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52817aa30ef645889ec653:
VANITAS STILL LIFE — Edwaert Collier.

A skull on an overturned crown, a globe, a lute and a jewellery box: wealth, power, knowledge and music, all passing. Collier, active in Leiden, London and Amsterdam, painted many vanitas around 1700.

#edwaertcollier #vanitas #stilllife #dutchpainting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52811cacb1d90fa9565abc:
CHALK GAMES — Arthur Leipzig, 1950.

Children drawing on the street in Prospect Place, Brooklyn, seen from above. Leipzig photographed New York's street games for years, a world of play now gone.

#arthurleipzig #chalkgames #brooklyn #streetphotography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281ef9405d21838297bf9:
SEASCAPES — Hiroshi Sugimoto, since 1980.

Sea and sky, divided exactly in the middle by the horizon, photographed with long exposures in many seas of the world. Each one looks the same and each one is different: water and air, as the first humans saw them.

#hiroshisugimoto #seascapes #photography #horizon #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528159816df342fc3870e2:
THE GARDEN OF EARTHLY DELIGHTS — Hieronymus Bosch, c. 1490–1510. Museo del Prado, Madrid.

A triptych: Eden on the left, hell on the right, and in the middle a garden full of naked figures, giant fruit and strange buildings. Closed, its shutters show the world in a glass sphere.

#hieronymusbosch #gardenofearthlydelights #museodelprado #triptych #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281b5b0b5def5652a7903:
DALÍ IN THE EGG — Philippe Halsman, 1942.

Dalí curled up as an embryo inside an egg, an image made with Halsman to illustrate Dalí's claim that he remembered life before birth. The start of a collaboration that lasted thirty years.

#philippehalsman #salvadordali #surrealism #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281e18ed8d0d1dc8304b9:
DAS SCHLAFZIMMER MEINER FRAU — Adolf Loos, 1903.

The bedroom Loos designed for his wife Lina: white fur on the floor, white linen draping the walls and the bed. A room almost without architecture, all softness and light, from the man who wrote against ornament.

#adolfloos #interior #vienna #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528106a2e8d47fda970f11:
THE ALLUVIAL VALLEY OF THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER — Harold Fisk, 1944.

Maps drawn for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, showing the old courses of the river in colored bands, one over the other. A geological survey that looks like a painting.

#haroldfisk #mississippi #maps #cartography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528145a391c0c849398ba6:
SPIRAL JETTY — Robert Smithson, 1970. Great Salt Lake, Utah.

A spiral of black basalt and earth, 460 metres long, running into the red water of the lake. It disappeared under the water for decades and reappeared white with salt.

#robertsmithson #spiraljetty #landart #greatsaltlake #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528172ae37eed87d7980a5:
CÉNOTAPHE DE NEWTON — Étienne-Louis Boullée, 1784.

A hollow sphere 150 metres high: by day, small holes in the vault turn the inside into a night sky; by night, a lamp inside becomes the sun. An architecture for an idea, never meant to be built.

#boullee #cenotaph #newton #visionaryarchitecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281968e28dc3cd1c3f248:
PIJÁK ABSINTU (THE ABSINTHE DRINKER) — Viktor Oliva, 1901. Café Slavia, Prague.

A man sits alone with his glass, and the green fairy appears on the table before him. The painting has hung for more than a century in the Café Slavia, facing the Vltava.

#viktoroliva #absinthe #cafeslavia #prague #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812ba3eafd4a255344f4:
ИВАНОВО ДЕТСТВО (IVAN'S CHILDHOOD) — Andrei Tarkovsky, 1962.

A twelve-year-old boy works as a scout on the Eastern Front. Tarkovsky's first feature cuts from the war to his dreams of light, water and his mother. It won the Golden Lion in Venice.

#andreitarkovsky #ivanschildhood #sovietcinema #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281459792f56180ed16ef:
FESTSPIELHAUS HELLERAU — Heinrich Tessenow, 1911–1912. Dresden.

Built in the garden city of Hellerau for Émile Jaques-Dalcroze's school of rhythmic movement. Inside, an empty hall with walls of white fabric lit from behind, designed with Alexander von Salzmann and Adolphe Appia, a space for bodies and light.

#heinrichtessenow #hellerau #festspielhaus #dresden #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528128a567da315b5d7142:
LE SERMENT DU JEU DE PAUME — Jacques-Louis David, 1791.

A huge drawing for a painting never finished: the deputies of the Third Estate swearing, in June 1789, not to separate until France had a constitution. The wind blows the curtains into the room.

#jacqueslouisdavid #sermentdujeudepaume #revolution #drawing #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281ada0fdc9cb1fe30397:
COURS D'ARCHITECTURE — Jacques-François Blondel, 1771–1777.

The lessons of the most influential architecture teacher of eighteenth-century Paris, published in nine volumes of text and plates. Boullée and Ledoux were among his students.

#blondel #coursdarchitecture #architecturetheory #engraving #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281cba13bd7e2e0e96173:
POOLSIDE GLAMOUR — Slim Aarons, 1970.

Two women by the pool of Richard Neutra's Kaufmann House in Palm Springs. Aarons spent his life photographing 'attractive people doing attractive things in attractive places'.

#slimaarons #kaufmannhouse #palmsprings #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f59548da53e5b66bcb:
SCUOLA DI ATENE — Raffaello Sanzio, 1509–1511. Vatican, Rome.

The philosophers of antiquity gathered under a vast vaulted hall, with Plato and Aristotle at the centre. Raphael gave Plato the face of Leonardo and painted himself at the edge, looking out at us.

#raffaello #schoolofathens #vaticanmuseums #renaissance #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528140a19dcdd513c451c2:
INVISIBLE CINEMA — Peter Kubelka, 1970. New York.

The cinema Kubelka designed for Anthology Film Archives: all black, with each seat hooded and screened on the sides, so that the viewer saw only the film and nothing else.

#peterkubelka #invisiblecinema #anthologyfilmarchives #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281559d51f5f484005c99:
CITY OF THE FUTURE — Harvey Wiley Corbett, 1913.

A drawing of a New York with streets on several levels: cars below, pedestrians on arcaded walkways above, and bridges between towers.

#harveywileycorbett #cityofthefuture #newyork #drawing #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a8b0b0d819e063a263:
ARRIVAL — Denis Villeneuve, 2016.

A linguist is asked to learn the language of visitors who write in circles of ink. As she learns it, her memory of time changes. Cinematography by Bradford Young.

#denisvilleneuve #arrival #bradfordyoung #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816aab12d5f48fe89a81:
STONY POINT, NEW YORK — Lee Friedlander, 1966.

Friedlander built his pictures out of the clutter of American streets: reflections, signs, poles and his own shadow crossing the frame, so that nothing stays in front of anything else.

#leefriedlander #streetphotography #americanphotography #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281cdb833c07ee486e44f:
CONICAL INTERSECT — Gordon Matta-Clark, 1975. Paris.

A cone cut through two seventeenth-century houses about to be demolished next to the site of the Centre Pompidou. For a few weeks, passers-by could look through the buildings to the sky.

#gordonmattaclark #conicalintersect #paris #anarchitecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281fa94bfc261201915df:
SYMBOL OF JOYCE — Constantin Brancusi, 1929.

Asked for a portrait of James Joyce, Brancusi drew a spiral and three lines. It was published in Joyce's Tales Told of Shem and Shaun.

#constantinbrancusi #jamesjoyce #drawing #portrait #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528103a7eff989490abb75:
FEAR AND LOATHING IN LAS VEGAS — Terry Gilliam, 1998.

Hunter S. Thompson's book on screen: a journalist and his lawyer cross the desert to Las Vegas in a convertible full of drugs. The carpets and walls of the casinos come alive.

#terrygilliam #fearandloathing #lasvegas #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528134be80e36675646552:
PIERROT LE FOU — Jean-Luc Godard, 1965.

Ferdinand leaves his life in Paris and runs away to the south with Marianne. Primary colors, comic strips, painted faces and the Mediterranean: Godard's road movie ends with dynamite.

#jeanlucgodard #pierrotlefou #nouvellevague #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816e8c61e7e53ddfc426:
SCANDIANO — Luigi Ghirri, 1971.

Ghirri returned again and again to the small towns of Emilia, where he was born. Billboards, painted walls and empty horizons, photographed in pale color as signs to be read.

#luigighirri #scandiano #emilia #italianphotography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528150b214c76890933d80:
FUN PALACE — Cedric Price with Joan Littlewood, 1961.

A 'laboratory of fun' that would never be finished: a steel frame with cranes that move rooms, floors and screens according to what people want to do. Never built, but the Centre Pompidou owes it a great deal.

#cedricprice #funpalace #joanlittlewood #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52819a924bf757466b33cc:
DIE TOTENINSEL — Arnold Böcklin, 1880. Kunstmuseum Basel.

A boat carries a figure in white toward a rocky island with cypresses. The first of five versions Böcklin painted; Rachmaninoff wrote a symphonic poem after it.

#arnoldbocklin #toteninsel #kunstmuseumbasel #symbolism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52811aa68fde54b1c15e6a:
PICKPOCKET — Robert Bresson, 1959.

A young man in Paris becomes a pickpocket almost as a philosophy. The thefts are filmed like a ballet of hands, with non-professional actors Bresson called 'models'.

#robertbresson #pickpocket #frenchcinema #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52811894a6f69fb2a2fa7a:
LE CITTÀ INVISIBILI — Italo Calvino, 1972.

Marco Polo describes to Kublai Khan fifty-five cities, each with a woman's name. Perhaps they are all Venice. A book about cities, memory and desire that architects never stopped reading.

#italocalvino #lecittainvisibili #invisiblecities #literature #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52811990ecd5d43eb9c078:
NEVE, EMILIA — Franco Fontana.

Fontana photographed the landscapes of Emilia as fields of pure color, flattened by the light into lines and planes. A photography close to abstract painting.

#francofontana #emilia #colorphotography #landscape #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281c1b3add75bb35fe941:
PERSONA — Ingmar Bergman, 1966.

An actress stops speaking; a nurse takes care of her on an island, and talks for both. Their faces end up merging into one. Cinematography by Sven Nykvist.

#ingmarbergman #persona #svennykvist #cinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528149a9f4f35aa297d48a:
STOP CITY — Dogma, 2007.

Pier Vittorio Aureli and Martino Tattara's answer to Archizoom's No-Stop City: a city made of a few huge, identical slabs set in an open field. Limiting the city instead of letting it spread.

#dogma #stopcity #piervittorioaureli #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52812687f7dcf25ce57b36:
LE DÉJEUNER DES CANOTIERS — Pierre-Auguste Renoir, 1880–81. The Phillips Collection, Washington.

Renoir's friends having lunch on the balcony of the Maison Fournaise on the Seine, near Chatou. Among them is Aline Charigot, holding a dog, whom he later married.

#pierreaugusterenoir #luncheonoftheboatingparty #phillipscollection #impressionism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d69d5ec90bc7de6dc2:
UNTITLED — Jean-Michel Basquiat, 1982.

1982 was Basquiat's most prolific year: skulls, crowns, words and anatomy painted at speed, in the language of the street.

#jeanmichelbasquiat #basquiat #neoexpressionism #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52813d84f9ec15d7736c4b:
VIA MEDINA, NAPLES — Thomas Struth, 1988.

From 'Unconscious Places', Struth's black and white photographs of streets in Europe, Japan and the United States, taken from the middle of the road at a calm distance. The city as it is, without event.

#thomasstruth #unconsciousplaces #napoli #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281ba99e2fd6e101b5b6c:
CARO DIARIO — Nanni Moretti, 1993.

Three chapters of a diary: Rome in August on a Vespa, the Aeolian islands, and an illness. The ride ends at the place in Ostia where Pasolini was killed.

#nannimoretti #carodiario #roma #italiancinema #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52813ba37ec5d09c5ff01f:
ZINNIA — NASA, ISS Expedition 46, 2016.

A zinnia grown on the International Space Station, photographed by Scott Kelly in January 2016. It grew in NASA's Veggie experiment, after the plants had almost died of mould.

#nasa #zinnia #iss #space #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818ca23ec37767e16409:
PIAZZA D'ITALIA — Charles Moore, 1976–1978. New Orleans.

A square for the Italian community of New Orleans: columns of every order in stainless steel and neon, fountains, and a map of Italy in stone running into a pool. Postmodernism in its most theatrical form.

#charlesmoore #piazzaditalia #neworleans #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f5aa69deaa2d580f3c:
ՆՌԱՆ ԳՈՒՅՆԸ (SAYAT NOVA / THE COLOR OF POMEGRANATES) — Sergei Parajanov, 1969.

The life of the eighteenth-century Armenian poet Sayat-Nova told in tableaux: almost still images of carpets, books, pomegranates and faces. The Soviet censors re-edited it and changed its title.

#sergeiparajanov #thecolorofpomegranates #sayatnova #armenia #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818a8667e0cf8f3e4f80:
PLA DE REFORMA I EIXAMPLE DE BARCELONA — Ildefons Cerdà, 1859.

The plan that extended Barcelona beyond its walls with a grid of blocks with cut corners. Cerdà also wrote the first general theory of urbanisation.

#ildefonscerda #eixample #barcelona #urbanism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281e5acd4d12328c6710a:
NODEULSEOM — Han Youngsoo, 1956. Seoul.

Han Youngsoo photographed Seoul in the years after the Korean War. On the island in the Han River, small figures cross a wide space of snow and light.

#hanyoungsoo #seoul #nodeulseom #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281cb8232fe0fd022cd5c:
VALLEY CURTAIN — Christo and Jeanne-Claude, 1970–1972. Rifle Gap, Colorado.

An orange nylon curtain 381 metres wide, hung across a valley in the Rocky Mountains. It stood for 28 hours before a gale forced its removal.

#christojeanneclaude #valleycurtain #colorado #landart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281caa480c8d16df5727c:
STEEL BEAMS AND LOTS OF DANGER — John Nye, 1988. Hong Kong.

A worker crouched on the end of a steel beam high above Victoria Harbour, wrench in hand. The city at his feet was growing upwards.

#johnnye #hongkong #construction #photography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281e9b6bde5d998e0f340:
U.S. HIGHWAY 1 — Allan D'Arcangelo.

D'Arcangelo painted the American road as the driver sees it: the asphalt, the signs and the line of the horizon reduced to flat color and hard edges.

#allandarcangelo #highway #popart #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281feac88f49129b2448b:
ASPHALT RUNDOWN — Robert Smithson, 1969. Rome.

A truck pours a load of hot asphalt down the slope of a quarry outside Rome and lets it run. Sculpture as an act of entropy.

#robertsmithson #asphaltrundown #roma #landart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d0a912e18ec068da22:
IDEALER DURCHSCHNITT DER ERDRINDE — after Alexander von Humboldt and others, c. 1850.

An ideal cross-section of the earth's crust, from Heinrich Berghaus's Physikalischer Atlas, compiled from the work of Nöggerath, Humboldt, Cotta and others. Mountains, volcanoes and strata in one imaginary landscape.

#humboldt #berghaus #geology #historyofscience #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528185a464c0972deb06aa:
THE COURSE OF EMPIRE: DESOLATION — Thomas Cole, 1836. New-York Historical Society.

The last of five paintings on the rise and fall of an imaginary empire. Here nothing is left: a column covered in ivy, ruined bridges and the moon over the water.

#thomascole #courseofempire #hudsonriverschool #ruins #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a2b26cf9a34d333e69:
FOUR SEASONS — Peter Max, 2000.

Max, the painter of 'Cosmic '60s' pop, made landscapes in thick strokes of color: water, reeds and sky, the same view repeated through the seasons.

#petermax #fourseasons #popart #painting #mnemotheca
